title: Classic Cappuccino with a Deep Foam Cap
summary: A double espresso under well-aerated steamed milk, finished with a domed cap of thick white foam, roughly a third each of espresso, milk and foam.

ingredients.note: about 120 ml ends up in the cup

steps.title: Pull the shot
steps.text: Pull a double espresso, 18 g in and about 40 ml out in 25-30 s, straight into the warm cup.

steps.title: Aerate
steps.text: Purge the wand, then hold its tip just under the surface of the cold milk and open the steam fully. Keep it high so the milk hisses and swells by about half, stopping once the jug no longer feels cold. Air goes in while the milk is cool, because cold proteins hold foam best.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Lower the tip slightly and let the milk spin until the jug is too hot to hold for more than a second, 60-65 °C. Hotter milk tastes flat and the foam collapses.

steps.title: Polish
steps.text: Tap the jug firmly on the counter and swirl to pop any large bubbles.

steps.title: Pour and top
steps.text: Pour the milk into the espresso, then spoon the thick foam over the top in a generous dome. Aim for roughly a third each of espresso, milk and foam.

tips: Start with very cold milk straight from the fridge; it gives you more time to build foam.
Whole milk makes the richest, most stable foam.
For an oat or soya version, choose a barista-style drink and check the label for allergens.
storage: Serve immediately; foam starts to separate within minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
